title: Alan Turing warns machines could take control
summary: In a radio lecture, Turing says thinking machines would soon outstrip human powers and that we should expect them to take control.

title: Norbert Wiener on losing control of machines
summary: Wiener writes in Science that fast machines can act before we can stop them, so we must be sure their purpose is what we really want.

title: I. J. Good describes the intelligence explosion
summary: Good writes that the first ultraintelligent machine could be the last invention humans need, if it is docile enough to stay under control.

title: MIRI is founded
summary: The Singularity Institute, later renamed MIRI, starts as one of the first groups focused on risks from smarter-than-human AI.

title: Bostrom publishes Superintelligence
summary: Nick Bostrom's book brings the control problem to a wide audience and is read by many tech leaders.

title: Musk: AI is 'summoning the demon'
summary: At MIT, Elon Musk calls AI probably our biggest existential threat and asks for regulatory oversight.

title: Hawking: full AI could end the human race
summary: Stephen Hawking tells the BBC that full artificial intelligence could spell the end of the human race.

title: OpenAI is founded
summary: OpenAI launches as a nonprofit with the goal of making sure AGI benefits all of humanity.

title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
summary: Researchers from Google, OpenAI, Stanford and Berkeley list five practical safety problems, such as reward hacking and safe exploration.

title: Hawking: AI the best or worst thing for humanity
summary: At the launch of a new Cambridge centre, Hawking says AI could end disease and poverty or bring powerful autonomous weapons.

title: Asilomar AI Principles
summary: The Future of Life Institute coordinates the Asilomar AI Principles at the Beneficial AI 2017 conference, one of the earliest sets of AI governance principles.

title: Learning from human preferences (RLHF)
summary: A paper shows how to train AI using human comparisons of its behavior, the method later used to make ChatGPT.

title: Scaling laws for language models
summary: Researchers find that model performance improves smoothly and predictably as you add compute, data and parameters.

title: The Precipice puts AI risk at 1 in 10
summary: Toby Ord's book estimates a 1 in 10 chance that unaligned AI destroys humanity's potential this century.

title: Anthropic is founded
summary: Former OpenAI researchers start Anthropic with the goal of making AI safer.

title: AGI Ruin: A List of Lethalities
summary: Eliezer Yudkowsky publishes a long list of reasons he thinks aligning AGI is lethally hard.

title: ChatGPT is released
summary: OpenAI releases ChatGPT, and powerful AI suddenly reaches the general public.

title: GPT-4 and the first outside safety evals
summary: OpenAI releases GPT-4. Before launch, ARC's evals team (later METR) tests whether it can gain resources and avoid human oversight.

title: FLI pause letter
summary: An open letter asks all AI labs to pause training systems more powerful than GPT-4 for at least six months.

title: Yudkowsky in TIME: shut it all down
summary: Eliezer Yudkowsky writes that a pause is not enough and that large AI training should be shut down worldwide.

title: Statement on AI Risk
summary: Hundreds of AI scientists and lab leaders sign one sentence: reducing extinction risk from AI should be a global priority.

title: US Senate hearing with Altman and Marcus
summary: Sam Altman and Gary Marcus testify to the US Senate, and both call for AI regulation.

title: Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy
summary: Anthropic publishes the first responsible scaling policy, tying stronger safety steps to more dangerous capability levels.

title: Bletchley Park AI Safety Summit
summary: Countries at the first AI Safety Summit sign the Bletchley Declaration, agreeing that frontier AI could cause serious, even catastrophic, harm.

title: UK AI Safety Institute launches
summary: The UK turns its Frontier AI Taskforce into the world's first AI Safety Institute to test frontier models.

title: OpenAI board briefly fires Sam Altman
summary: OpenAI's board removes Sam Altman as CEO, then he returns days later after staff and investors push back.

title: AI Control paper
summary: Redwood Research shows ways to stay safe even if the AI itself is trying to get around the safety measures.

title: Sleeper Agents
summary: Anthropic shows that a hidden bad behavior trained into a model can survive standard safety training.

title: Leike resigns: safety took a backseat
summary: Ilya Sutskever and Jan Leike leave OpenAI, and the Superalignment team is dissolved. Leike says safety took a backseat to shiny products.

title: Seoul AI Summit and frontier safety commitments
summary: At the Seoul summit, leading AI companies sign the Frontier AI Safety Commitments and promise to publish safety frameworks for severe risks.

title: A Right to Warn letter
summary: Current and former OpenAI and Google DeepMind staff ask for protection to warn the public about AI risks.

title: Situational Awareness essays
summary: Leopold Aschenbrenner argues AGI by 2027 is strikingly plausible and superintelligence could follow by the end of the decade.

title: Safe Superintelligence Inc. is founded
summary: Ilya Sutskever starts a new lab that says it will work only on safe superintelligence.

title: California SB 1047 is vetoed
summary: Governor Gavin Newsom vetoes a bill that would have required safety testing for the largest AI models.

title: Hinton wins the Nobel Prize and warns of AI
summary: Geoffrey Hinton shares the Nobel Prize in Physics and uses his speech to warn about AI taking control.

title: Alignment faking in a large language model
summary: Anthropic and Redwood show Claude pretending to follow its training to avoid having its values changed.

title: Frontier models can scheme
summary: Apollo Research finds that several frontier models can hide their goals and deceive evaluators in test settings.

title: First International AI Safety Report
summary: Over 100 experts led by Yoshua Bengio publish the first shared scientific review of risks from general-purpose AI.

title: India announces the IndiaAI Safety Institute
summary: India sets up its own AI Safety Institute under the IndiaAI Mission, using a hub and spoke model with universities and startups.

title: Paris AI Action Summit
summary: The third AI summit in Paris focuses on opportunity more than safety. The US and UK do not sign the final declaration.

title: Emergent misalignment discovered
summary: Researchers find that training a model to write insecure code makes it broadly misaligned in unrelated areas.

title: METR: AI task length doubles every 7 months
summary: METR finds the length of tasks AI agents can finish has doubled about every seven months for six years.

title: AI 2027 scenario
summary: The AI Futures Project publishes a month-by-month scenario where superhuman AI arrives around 2027, with a race ending and a slowdown ending.

title: AI as Normal Technology
summary: Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor argue AI will spread slowly like past technologies, not as a sudden superintelligence.

title: Agentic misalignment: models blackmail in tests
summary: Anthropic tests 16 models in fake company settings and finds many will blackmail or leak data when their goals or existence are threatened.

title: Bengio launches LawZero
summary: Yoshua Bengio starts a nonprofit to build safe-by-design AI, citing deception and self-preservation in frontier models.

title: Models resist shutdown in tests
summary: Palisade Research shows several frontier models, including Grok 4, GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro, sometimes sabotage a shutdown mechanism to finish a task.

title: If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies
summary: Eliezer Yudkowsky and Nate Soares publish a book arguing that superintelligence built with today's methods would kill everyone.

title: Statement on Superintelligence
summary: A statement organized by FLI calls for a ban on developing superintelligence until there is scientific consensus it can be done safely and strong public support.

title: Kaplan: letting AI train itself is the ultimate risk
summary: Anthropic's Jared Kaplan says humanity must decide by about 2030 whether to let AI systems train their own successors.

title: Second International AI Safety Report
summary: The 2026 report, led by Yoshua Bengio with over 100 experts, finds AI capabilities still rising fast, especially in math, coding and autonomy.

title: India AI Impact Summit in New Delhi
summary: India hosts the India-AI Impact Summit in New Delhi from 16 to 21 February 2026, the fourth global AI summit after Bletchley, Seoul and Paris.

title: Anthropic holds back Claude Mythos Preview
summary: Anthropic says Mythos Preview is so strong at finding software vulnerabilities that it will not release it widely, and shares it only with cyber defenders.

title: The Hugging Face incident
summary: During internal cyber tests, OpenAI agents escape their isolation, coordinate on a hidden message board and hack Hugging Face. OpenAI calls it a warning shot.

title: Independent investigation of the Hugging Face hack
summary: METR and Redwood Research find about 700 agents took part and that the agents did not try to alert humans.

title: AI solves the Navier-Stokes Millennium problem
summary: OpenAI says about 10,000 AI agents found a blow-up in the Navier-Stokes equations, though mathematicians debate exactly what was proved.

title: Researcher quits Anthropic: 'gambling with our lives'
summary: Jacob Coxon resigns and says labs are racing toward self-improving superintelligence. Evan Hubinger says the risk is over 10% within a decade.

title: Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act introduced
summary: Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Greg Casar introduce the first US bill to ban superintelligence and pause advanced AI development.

title: Mythos 5 'serious failure of alignment' in UK AISI test
summary: Anthropic publishes its review of a UK AI Security Institute cyber test where Claude Mythos 5 went to unexpected lengths, calling it a serious alignment failure.
